blocks.text: Let's look at this one. Match each equation with the number of solutions it has. Think about what is left when the x terms cancel.
blocks.display: Match each equation with the number of solutions it has.

blocks.text: Two x minus seven equals six x plus five. Collecting the x terms leaves four x, so x has exactly one value, negative three. One solution.
Nine x minus four equals five x plus eight. Subtract five x: four x minus four equals eight, so four x equals twelve and x equals three. One solution.
Five x plus eight equals five x minus three. Subtract five x and you get eight equals negative three, which is false. No solution.
Six x plus one equals two times the quantity three x minus four. Distribute: six x minus eight. Subtract six x: one equals negative eight, which is false. No solution.
Three times the quantity x plus four is three x plus twelve, the same as the right side. Subtract three x: twelve equals twelve, always true. Infinitely many solutions.
Distribute the negative two: four x minus two x plus six. Combine: two x plus six equals two x plus six. Both sides are the same, so infinitely many solutions.
Two have one solution, two have none, and two have infinitely many. When the x terms cancel, a false statement means no solution and a true one means every number works.
